week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent.

new.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
new.readme: An agent skill for hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: single-user and concurrent decode startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: Compute the theoretical ceiling. Measure against interleaved controls. Log every result, including the failures. Gate on long-context retrieval.

new.readme: LLMs drive today’s chatbots and agents, but chatbots long predate them. new.description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
new.readme: tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser. Small: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included. Fast: about 70x real time on four CPU threads. Two voices: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz. Runs anywhere: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web. Open: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch. Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.

new.readme: Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone. Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page.
